main_text.p: in ista exercet, etiamsi oculis minime sit conspicuus, & tantum ratiocinio cognoscatur, & effectu suo fiat manifestus. Ubi certe agnoscit Hippocrates τῇ ὄψει ἀφανὲς, oculis inconspicuum, τῷ λογισμῷ φανερὸν, ratione conspicuum esse: etenim ὅσα γὰρ τῶν τῆς ὁμματῶν ὄψιν ἐκφεύγει, τούτα τῇ τῆς γνώμης ὄψει κεκρύπτηται; Quaecunque enim oculorum conspectum effugiunt, ea mentis oculis obtinentur & superantur. Hipp. de Arte xix. 9. Planè eodem modo, imò à priori Sylvius Praxeos suae p. 109. probat effervescentiam fieri in intestino duodeno, his verbis talē, hoc est, quovis modo vel gradu acidum pancreatis succum impossibile est commisceri cum Bile amara & sale volatili abundante, quin mox excitetur inde effervescentia infinitis ex Chymia & aliunde petitis exemplis confirmanda. page.notes: The Greek passages are printed in Greek and were read from a small, slightly blurred scan; the exact accents and some letters are uncertain and may differ from the printer's text. The first Greek phrase ("τῇ ὄψει ἀφανὲς") and the phrase "τῆς γνώμης ὄψει κεκρύπτηται" are the least certain. The Latin is clear. The catchword "con-" is printed at the lower right.
